turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Mr Keller's here for his repeats. Pressure 142 over 86, pulse 74, sats 98 on air, and the chemist list is on the screen.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sorry, that pressure again? The computer's away with the fairies.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): 142 over 86, pulse 74.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ta. Just the usual repeats?
[SEG0005] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Repeats, and he wants a stronger painkiller. The right knee. I'm June, his wife.
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): How long's the right knee been sore?
[SEG0007] person_4 (PATIENT): Two.
[SEG0008] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Years, he means. Nearer five, I'd say, from when he gave up bowls. It never came good.
[SEG0009] person_2 (DOCTOR): Roughly two to five years on that right knee, I won't fight the file over it. Worse lately, with walking?
[SEG0010] person_4 (PATIENT): Yeah.
[SEG0011] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And he wakes from the pain, two or three times a night.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sleeping alright?
[SEG0013] person_4 (PATIENT): Panadol.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): I meant sleep, not Panadol. Are you sleeping alright?
[SEG0015] person_4 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Swelling, fever, chest pain?
[SEG0017] person_4 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Short of breath?
[SEG0019] person_4 (PATIENT): Knee.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Breathing, I said. Any shortness of breath?
[SEG0021] person_4 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): Heartburn? Black stools?
[SEG0023] person_4 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Panadol, say the dose again, I lost the tab.
[SEG0025] person_4 (PATIENT): Two.
[SEG0026] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Two of the 500 milligram tablets, four times a day, by mouth, for that knee. I set them out.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): So one gram four times a day. And the Mobic?
[SEG0028] person_4 (PATIENT): Fifteen.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fifteen milligrams once a day?
[SEG0030] person_4 (PATIENT): Yeah. Fifteen.
[SEG0031] person_1 (NURSE): Chemist list says meloxicam 7.5 milligrams once daily. Dispensed last month. Not fifteen.
[SEG0032] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He takes the one he calls fifteen. I've no idea which note is right.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Then the dose is unsettled. Every morning without fail?
[SEG0034] person_4 (PATIENT): Suppose.
[SEG0035] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Some mornings it's still in the glass when he heads out. I can't say he takes it as he's meant to.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Suppose and a tablet left behind, so adherence is anyone's guess. Somac still?
[SEG0037] person_4 (PATIENT): Yeah.
[SEG0038] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Pantoprazole 20 milligrams every morning, for his stomach, with the Mobic. My perindopril is not his, if you saw that name.
[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): Ignore the perindopril. Any medicine allergies?
[SEG0040] person_4 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): What stronger tablet were you after?
[SEG0042] person_4 (PATIENT): Endone.
[SEG0043] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): A mate gave him one Endone once and he slept. He reckons the Panadol isn't enough.

[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): I am not prescribing Endone, not off one tablet from a mate. Thinking it through, the pain might be the osteoarthritis we've already got on file for that knee, or it might be referred from the hip. I will not conclude it's nerve pain today.
[SEG0045] person_4 (PATIENT): Hip's fine.
[SEG0046] person_2 (DOCTOR): Maybe. I'm not settling the cause yet. No redness on the right knee, it's not warm, and it creaks when you bend. Not a hot joint.
[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): The kidney blood test they did, what was said?
[SEG0048] person_4 (PATIENT): Borderline.
[SEG0049] person_2 (DOCTOR): And when was that?
[SEG0050] person_4 (PATIENT): Dunno.
[SEG0051] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sometime last year. Just borderline. We never wrote a number down.

[SEG0052] person_2 (DOCTOR): No date and no figure, so that result can't carry a decision. I'll renew paracetamol one gram four times a day and pantoprazole 20 milligrams each morning. I won't start Endone, and I won't increase the Mobic while you and the chemist list disagree.
[SEG0053] person_2 (DOCTOR): Use your stick if the footpath's rough. If the knee goes red and hot, come straight back. Otherwise I'll see you in three months.
[SEG0054] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): So no Mobic script today?
[SEG0055] person_2 (DOCTOR): Correct. Ring the chemist, confirm 7.5 or 15, and we'll write it after that. Not this afternoon.
[SEG0056] person_1 (NURSE): I'll print the Panadol and the Somac, and book the three-month visit at the desk.

spec.situation: Routine repeat-prescription review at a small clinic with a pharmacy technician present; patient wants a stronger painkiller; tablet names and doses are discussed in detail, one dose is read from the pharmacy list and differs from the patient's own; doctor declines the stronger medicine.
features: patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.

doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.
test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.
ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

omissions.text: Oxygen saturation was 98% on air/room air.
Sleep was not alright / patient reported poor sleep when specifically asked.
Meloxicam dose is recorded as current medication without noting that the dose is unsettled and current use itself is uncertain because adherence is unreliable.
Pantoprazole was specifically stated to be taken with the Mobic/for stomach protection.
Family member stated that perindopril listed was her medication, not the patient's, and the doctor said to ignore perindopril.

The doctor explicitly said he was not prescribing Endone because it was requested after the patient had taken one tablet given by a mate; this history of taking someone else's Endone once is not recorded.
The doctor said he was not settling the cause of the pain yet / diagnosis not concluded today.
Borderline kidney blood test was sometime last year, but with no number available.
No meloxicam/Mobic prescription was issued today; the doctor confirmed 'no Mobic script today' and 'not this afternoon'.
